notesStmt.note: This manuscript most likely dates to the days just prior to the poem's initial publication. No image of the verso is currently available.

"Ah, Not This Granite Dead and Cold" was originally published in the Philadelphia Press on February 22, 1885. Whitman later made minor revisions and republished the poem under the title "Washington's Monument, February, 1885" in November Boughs (1888) and in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891–1892).

lg.head: Beyond this Ah, not theis granite dead and cold.
lg.l: Beyond this Ah not theis granite dead and cold,

Far, far far from this base and shaft expanding,—the
round zones circling, comprehending,

l.add: No lurid fame exceptional, nor monstrous intellect, nor freedom's conquest's c domination

lg.l:
Thou, Washington, art ‸all the world's, humanity's,
Freedom's, Law's—not yours alone, America

l.del:
Thy fame, (no lurid fame exceptional for the nor
intellect, nor conquest's domination,)

By deathless waves of emanation the race's
common ownership,

lg.l:
Europe's, ‸as well, in castle or in cot laborer's cot—the
Arab's in his tent—the African's,

Old Asia's there with venerable smile seated
amid the past,

(Greets the antique the hero new? 'tis but the
same—the eternal heart and arm—the
heir legitimate

Courage, alertness, patience, hope, the same—
e'en in defeat defeated not, the same;)

l.add: No lurid fame exceptional, nor monstrous intellect, nor conquest's domination;)

lg.l:
Through teeming cities' streets, indoors or out,
factories or farms,

Where'er ship sails or house is built on land,
or night or day,

Now, or to come, or past—where patriot
bra wills existed or exist

l.add: Wherever Freedom, pois'd by toleration, sway'd by Law,

lg.l: Rising or risen, of thee are monuments. there are is thy monumentst
